# PR #165 correctness verdict

**PASS-WITH-NOTES** at `46712bbe95cadc6b10d38cae6e8871e4c70fedc6`.

Every live daemon-driven Copilot/Claude seat launch receives the intended tool filter. Spawn, resumed launch and revive share the builder; the diff adds only the relevant argv tokens and preserves other launch controls.

## Launch-path trace

- `launch_seat` enters `launch_seat_locked` (`daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1327-1344`). The latter always builds SpawnPlanInput, including executable override and resume, through build_spawn_plan (`:1471-1483`).
- Revive reconstructs SpawnRequest from prior launch facts and passes resume to that same locked path (`http/revive.rs:411-439`). It does not reuse a separate unfiltered argv.
- The builder unconditionally adds `--no-ask-user` beside Copilot's `--yolo`, and `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` beside Claude's existing permission flag, after the harness-native resume spelling (`harnesses/src/spawn.rs:145-215`).
- observed_launch_command preserves the complete plan.args after its wrapper separator; the wrapper command reaches tmux.new_window (`spawn.rs:255-292`; `http/mod.rs:1530-1545`).

I traced the alternate TS builders. buildControlSpawnCommand has no non-test consumer beyond its declaration/documentation. The live buildSpawnCommand accepts only pi/omp and does not provide another Copilot/Claude launch path. Adoption binds an already-running process; it does not call the argv builder or create a window.

## Preserved argv and flag meaning

The production diff contains only one new Copilot token and two Claude tokens. PIJ identity/correlator environment, binary selection, resume spelling, model/effort, Copilot fusion/default context handling and refusal, Claude --settings/crossSessionInbound stamping, and existing permission flags are unchanged. Pi/OMP/Codex argv are unchanged.

This build's Copilot documentation explicitly defines --no-ask-user as disabling ask_user while still allowing questions in replies. It does not change tool/path/URL approval policy. Claude's filter names only AskUserQuestion; it does not replace the existing --settings or --dangerously-skip-permissions arguments.

## Proof

Exact-head CI **42411875834** passed. Its JUnit has **2164 cases, zero failures/errors**, including:

- the new spawn/resume tool-filter test for both harnesses;
- exact all-harness argv vectors;
- each harness's resume spelling;
- Claude settings/acceptance stamping;
- executable override and absent-option preservation;
- fusion context/effort cases and wrapper argv transparency;
- the HTTP revive/resume integration control.

The source/header pin remained detached, clean and equal to the remote head; GitHub reports CLEAN/ready. No migration or recurring launch/poll/timer was added.

The author reports installed-CLI flag acceptance and three closed canaries: flagged Copilot, flagged Claude and unflagged Claude control. I did not launch/re-run them or inspect private logs. The comparative Claude replies and Copilot registration/tool-availability report are author evidence, not a fresh machine tool-manifest observation by this reviewer.

No local product builds/tests, mutations, canaries or interactive questions were performed.

## Notes

- **N001:** adoption, hand-started sessions and already-running seats do not acquire startup flags retroactively. An affected existing seat needs an appropriately flagged relaunch/resume; extension reload alone is not this tool filter.
- **N002:** this removes the named model-question tool, not every possible CLI dialog such as trust/startup UI. The existing permission settings and F47 detector remain separate controls. Zero ask_user calls alone would not prove tool absence; retain the documented flag semantics and explicit availability/control evidence.

No blocking correctness finding. Security/performance acceptance remains independently owned.
